patients.summary: Warehouse logistics coordinator in long-term recovery from opioid use disorder on naltrexone, with PTSD on sertraline and hepatitis C cured in 2021. Reinfected with hepatitis C in 2024 and cured again with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir; in spring 2026 develops pancytopenia, referred to hematology, where a marrow shows aplastic anemia.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
42-year-old man transferring care; his former primary care office is closing its panel. Came with his pill bottles.

Hepatitis C: diagnosed years ago in the setting of injection use. Treated with a 12-week antiviral course in 2021 through his old office, told he was cured. No symptoms now.

Opioid use disorder: in sustained remission. No injection or other use in years by his account. Goes to his recovery program meetings several times a week. Naltrexone 50 mg daily by mouth, takes it every morning, no side effects. Old prescriber was the prior PCP; I will take it over.

PTSD: on sertraline 100 mg for years. Sleep is ok most nights, occasional bad stretch around anniversaries.

Also takes vitamin D3 2000 units daily on his own.

PSH: appendectomy at 16. Left femur ORIF at 28 after a car crash, no hardware problems.
FH: father had alcohol use disorder with cirrhosis. Mother has hypertension and hypothyroidism. Younger brother has hepatitis C.
SH: logistics coordinator at a warehouse, day shift. Smoked for years, quit in 2021. No alcohol. Single.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. Vitals as charted. Sclerae anicteric. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar, no organomegaly. Old lateral thigh scar on the left. No edema. Skin without track marks or rash. Mood good, affect full.

PHQ-9 4.

Assessment/plan:
1. History of hepatitis C, treated 2021: checking HCV RNA to confirm cure on our end. Requesting old records.
2. OUD in sustained remission: continue naltrexone 50 mg daily. Encouraged him to keep going to meetings.
3. PTSD: stable on sertraline 100 mg, continue.
4. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, HIV screen today. Tdap given (none on record). Colon screening at 45.
RTC 4-5 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brian, all of your bloodwork from Monday looks good. Kidney and liver tests are normal, blood counts are normal, cholesterol is fine. The hepatitis C virus test came back not detected, which confirms the 2021 treatment worked. HIV screen negative. Nothing to change. Take care.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records packet from the patient's previous primary care office, received by fax, 38 pages.

Problem list on their last summary: hepatitis C (treated), opioid use disorder in remission, PTSD.
Medications: naltrexone 50 mg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: none known.

Hepatitis C: genotype and baseline labs from 2021 in the packet. 12-week antiviral regimen completed in 2021. Post-treatment viral load undetectable, documented as sustained virologic response.

Other: tobacco cessation counseling 2021, patient quit that year. Routine metabolic panels and blood counts 2021-2022 within normal limits.

Reviewed and filed by PCP. Consistent with history given at visit.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after his shift for flu and the 2023-24 COVID shot. No fever today, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, felt fine, left.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check-in. Work busy with the holiday freight volume, long days but manageable. Still at meetings, three a week. Taking naltrexone daily without missed doses. No cravings to speak of. Sertraline steady; sleeping alright.

Vitals as charted. Calm, good eye contact, organized.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P: OUD in sustained remission, continue naltrexone 50 mg. PTSD stable, continue sertraline 100 mg. 90-day refills sent. Physical next summer.
